overview: Birla Mandir is one of the most prominent Hindu temples in Hyderabad, Telangana. Dedicated to Lord Sri Venkateswara (Balaji), the temple stands atop Naubat Pahad, overlooking the city and Hussain Sagar Lake. Constructed entirely of white Rajasthan marble (about 2,000 tons), it is renowned for its peaceful atmosphere, architectural beauty, and panoramic views of Hyderabad. Built by the Birla Foundation (1970–1976) under the guidance of Swami Ranganathananda of the Ramakrishna Mission, it blends Dravidian, Rajasthani, and Utkala architectural styles. Every year, thousands of devotees and tourists visit to seek blessings and admire its magnificent craftsmanship.
summary: Birla Mandir, atop Naubat Pahad in Khairatabad, Hyderabad, is a prominent Vaishnavite temple dedicated to Lord Sri Venkateswara (Balaji). Built entirely of pure white Rajasthan marble by the Birla Foundation between 1970 and 1976 under Swami Ranganathananda of the Ramakrishna Mission, it harmoniously blends Dravidian, Rajasthani and Utkala architecture, with intricate carvings from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Bhagavad Gita. The sanctum houses an ~11-foot granite idol of Lord Venkateswara, with additional shrines to Padmavati, Andal, Shiva, Lakshmi, Ganesha, Hanuman and Sai Baba. It is a major centre of Vaishnavite worship and a popular tourist landmark overlooking Hussain Sagar.

history.content: Birla Mandir was built by the Birla Foundation under the guidance of Swami Ranganathananda of the Ramakrishna Mission. Construction began in 1970 and was completed in 1976. Approximately 2,000 tons of pure white marble from Rajasthan were used. The temple was established to provide devotees with a serene place of worship in the heart of Hyderabad while promoting India's rich cultural and spiritual heritage.

sthala_puranam: Built with 2,000 tons of white marble, blending Dravidian, Rajasthani, and Odia styles. The idol of Lord Venkateswara is 11 ft tall under a lotus canopy. The hill 'Naubath Pahad' was historically used by Mughals/Nizams for drum proclamations.
religious_significance: Birla Mandir is considered an important centre of Vaishnavite worship in Telangana. Devotees believe that worshipping Lord Venkateswara here brings prosperity, peace, wisdom, and success. The temple serves as a place of meditation and spiritual reflection for devotees from different parts of India.
spiritual_significance: An important centre of Vaishnavite worship in Telangana, the temple is a place of meditation and spiritual reflection. Devotees believe worship of Lord Venkateswara here brings prosperity, peace, wisdom and success.
healing_beliefs: Blessings of prosperity, peace, wisdom and success through worship of Lord Venkateswara
miracles_and_devotee_experiences: Devotees report peace, fulfillment of wishes, and transformative calm. The temple is unique for having no bells, encouraging meditation. Panoramic views of Hussain Sagar Lake add to the spiritual experience.
architecture: The temple is built entirely from white marble and showcases a harmonious blend of Dravidian (South Indian), Rajasthani (North Indian), and Utkala (Odisha) architectural styles. The sanctum houses a magnificent granite idol of Lord Venkateswara, standing about 11 feet tall. Intricate carvings depicting scenes from the Ramayana, Mahabharata, and Bhagavad Gita adorn the temple walls and pillars. The elevated Naubat Pahad location offers breathtaking views of Hussain Sagar Lake, Tank Bund, and the Hyderabad city skyline.

The location atop Naubat Pahad provides panoramic views. Only downside is the crowd on weekends and the limited parking space. Photography is not allowed inside, so plan your visit accordingly.'

travel_guide.en: Birla Mandir is on Naubat Pahad in Khairatabad, central Hyderabad, well connected by TSRTC buses, taxis, metro feeder services and app-based cabs. The nearest metro is Lakdikapul, the nearest railway stations are Hyderabad Deccan, Secunderabad and Kacheguda, and the nearest airport is Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, about thirty kilometres away. The temple is open from 7:00 AM to 12:00 PM and 3:00 PM to 9:00 PM, with a midday break.
